name: Mepitiostane (Thioderon)

lead: Mepitiostane (Thioderon) is an oral steroid the body converts into epitiostanol, combining antiestrogen activity with weak anabolic and androgenic activity. Bodybuilders discuss it for a drier, leaner contest look.

Epitiostanol binds the estrogen receptor as an antagonist and the androgen receptor as an agonist, which is the basis for the less-water, harder-muscle idea. In Japan it has been marketed for breast cancer and for anemia in kidney failure, with a phase III trial against medroxyprogesterone acetate in breast cancer. Animal studies show the intact molecule travels via intestinal lymph, letting part of the dose bypass first-pass liver metabolism. No human study has tested it for appearance.

paras: It is an oral prescription drug in Japan. Physique use is based on discussion in bodybuilding circles rather than documented routines.

Wikipedia reports a high rate of virilizing effects in women, such as acne, hirsutism and voice changes. It is prescription-only where sold, and sports authorities prohibit it; urine tests for its metabolites exist.

chain: Less water and fat, drier muscle look
angle.text: Mepitiostane is discussed for a drier, leaner look: it converts to epitiostanol, which blocks estrogen action and weakly activates androgen receptors. It is used medically in Japan for breast cancer and renal anemia; no appearance studies exist.

lead: Mepitiostane (brand name Thioderon) is an orally active synthetic steroid of the dihydrotestosterone group that acts as an antiestrogen and a weak anabolic-androgenic steroid. It is a prodrug, meaning it is converted in the body to epitiostanol, the active compound. [1] Because it is a pill rather than an injection, it is the form of the pair that bodybuilding discussion tends to mention, usually as the parent of the over-the-counter product epistane. [2]

In Japan it has been marketed for breast cancer and for anemia associated with kidney failure. [1] Published clinical work includes a phase III comparison with medroxyprogesterone acetate in advanced postmenopausal breast cancer, a study in hemodialysis patients with ACE-inhibitor-related anemia, and a case report of a presumed meningioma that regressed during treatment. [3][4][5]

No published human study has examined mepitiostane for bodybuilding or other appearance goals. The appearance rationale offered in forums is its anabolic classification and estrogen-blocking activity, and it features in anti-doping analytical literature. [6][2]

paras: Wikipedia states that mepitiostane is marketed in Japan as an antineoplastic agent for breast cancer and is also used for anemia in renal failure. [1]

A 1985 phase III trial compared oral high-dose medroxyprogesterone acetate with mepitiostane in advanced postmenopausal breast cancer. [3] A 1989 study in chronic hemodialysis patients examined whether adding mepitiostane prevented the worsening of anemia seen with ACE inhibitors such as captopril and enalapril. [4] A 2000 neurosurgical case report described regression of a presumed meningioma during treatment with the drug. [5]

A 1978 randomized, double-blind trial by the Japanese Cooperative Group of Hormonal Treatment for Breast Cancer compared oral mepitiostane in 50 patients with advanced breast cancer with fluoxymesterone in 48 controls. Objective tumour regression occurred in 34 percent of the mepitiostane group and 47.7 percent of the fluoxymesterone group, a difference the authors reported as not significant, with significantly less hepatotoxicity in the mepitiostane group. [7]

A 1989 Japanese case report described a 71-year-old woman with hypoplastic leukemia who entered complete remission after treatment with mepitiostane following several failed regimens, and remained in remission for over 15 months; the authors suggested androgen therapy may help some patients with this condition. [8] A 2014 case series reported regression of intracranial meningiomas in older patients treated with the antiestrogen. [9]

Mepitiostane is the 1-methoxycyclopentyl ether of epitiostanol. After it is absorbed, it is converted to epitiostanol, which antagonizes the estrogen receptor and also has androgenic activity. Wikipedia compares its antiestrogen action to that of tamoxifen. [1]

Rat studies found that when mepitiostane was placed in the small intestine, about a third of the radioactivity appeared in thoracic duct lymph, mostly as unchanged drug carried in chylomicrons and VLDL. The portal blood fraction was extensively taken up by the liver. The authors concluded that lymphatic absorption lets mepitiostane avoid part of first-pass metabolism. [10]

Further rat work found that the extent of lymphatic absorption depended on the oily vehicle used, with long-chain triglycerides such as triolein and sesame oil giving the greatest uptake, and that bile also affected absorption. [11][12] Comparison with epitiostanol found that the prodrug was transferred into lymph far more than epitiostanol itself. [13]
Wikipedia reports a high rate of virilizing effects in women, including acne, hirsutism and voice changes. [1]

A 1989 clinical study of 76 male hemodialysis patients found lower testosterone in 23 patients who received anabolic steroids (mepitiostane or nandrolone decanoate), about 205 versus 450 ng/dl in those who did not, with no significant difference in gonadotropins or prolactin. Testosterone rose in three patients after stopping mepitiostane, and one patient with complete aspermia recovered a sperm count after discontinuation and hCG administration. The authors advised that mepitiostane or its analogues be prescribed carefully for young male patients. [14] Wikipedia notes that the related compound methylepitiostanol, which is orally active, carries a risk of hepatotoxicity. [1]

The World Anti-Doping Agency prohibits mepitiostane. A 2015 analytical study described a liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry method to detect its urinary metabolites, epitiostanol sulfoxide and epitiostanol, for sports drug testing. [6]

On the T Nation forum, mepitiostane is described as the parent of epistane and its clones in a prohormone thread, and another poster lists it among oral anabolics that are not 17-alpha-alkylated. [2][15] One poster who asked about epistane quoted the common description that the supplement acts "SERM-like", and added that the parent steroid epitiostanol is documented in studies as suppressing tumour growth; another corrected that mepitiostane and epitiostanol have human medical use while methylepitiostanol is a designer steroid with no approved medicinal use. [16][17] These discussions concern a related product rather than data on mepitiostane for physique outcomes.
No studies of mepitiostane for muscle gain, body composition or other appearance outcomes were found. Human studies concern disease settings.

In breast cancer, a 1985 phase III trial randomized 47 patients to high-dose medroxyprogesterone acetate and 40 to mepitiostane. Objective responses were 40.4 percent and 35.0 percent respectively, and among those with bone metastases 6 of 19 versus 2 of 13; the authors listed improved performance status, appetite and a myeloprotective effect as other merits of medroxyprogesterone. [3] The 1978 cooperative-group trial against fluoxymesterone is described above. [7]

In 12 chronic hemodialysis patients, hematocrit fell by 10 percent or more in 6 who received captopril or enalapril, and adding mepitiostane significantly improved the anemia without changes in circulating erythropoietin or renin-angiotensin indices. [4] The hypogonadism study, the leukemia case report, the 2000 meningioma case report and the 2014 meningioma series complete the human literature. [5][8][9][14]
